findings.title: Mutating and costly commands lack consistent authorization
findings.file: commands_advanced.py, commands_sales.py, commands_visibility.py, commands_concept.py, commands_ai.py, commands_market.py
findings.line: commands_advanced.py:108; commands_sales.py:124,159,566; commands_visibility.py:23,44; commands_concept.py:14; commands_ai.py:724,1701; commands_market.py:101
findings.explanation: Only commands_supercomputer.py consistently uses BOT_OWNERS. !snapshot_now, !sales_backfill, !sales_post_now, !visibility_seed, !visibility_run, !concept, !brainstorm, !ai_debug, and !dbtest have no owner/admin check. Several write the database, call live Roblox APIs, or spend AI quota.
findings.reproduction: Static source inspection plus runtime registry inspection. BOT_OWNERS references occur only in commands_supercomputer.py (lines 31, 1138, 1166, 1187, 1215, 1567, 1765, 1948, 2220) and vanta_conversation.py. No global before_invoke/check guard was found.
findings.production_impact: Any user able to issue commands in the bot's Discord context can trigger API jobs, write visibility/sales data, spend AI quota, or print diagnostics.
findings.recommended_correction: Add a central owner/admin authorization guard, explicitly classify every command as public/read-only, user-owned, or operator-only, and rate-limit costly AI commands.
findings.verification: Attempt each operator-only command as a non-owner in a disposable Discord test harness; verify rejection before any DB/API call. Add a command-metadata test that fails when an operator-only command lacks the guard.

findings.title: !ai_debug exposes partial API key material without an owner gate
findings.explanation: The command prints the first 8 characters of GEMINI_API_KEY and first 10 characters of OPENROUTER_API_KEY, plus key length, to any caller. It also performs live AI provider test calls.
findings.reproduction: Static inspection of commands_ai.py:1706-1714. Runtime registry confirms ai_debug is registered without an owner check.
findings.production_impact: Information disclosure of secret prefixes and key length; unnecessary AI provider calls; potential quota abuse.
findings.recommended_correction: Make the command owner-only and report only configured/not configured, provider model, and redacted health status. Never print any secret prefix.
findings.verification: Non-owner invocation must be denied; owner output must contain no substring of configured keys. Add a unit test with fake keys.

findings.title: Heuristic score is presented as success probability with action directives
findings.explanation: predict_success sums hand-selected factors and returns 'probability'. format_prediction calls it a '% probability' and prints directives such as 'Attack immediately' and 'Launch within 7 days'. The command does not state that the score is uncalibrated or a heuristic.
findings.reproduction: Source inspection; run !predict in a test harness with a fixed fixture and observe the 'probability' and action wording. No calibration/backtest evidence is attached to the score.
findings.production_impact: Users may treat an unvalidated heuristic as a statistical probability and make launch decisions on it.
findings.recommended_correction: Rename to heuristic opportunity score, remove probability language and action directives, label limitations, and require calibration/backtest evidence before using probability language.
findings.verification: Assert output contains no 'probability' or directive language; test that a label explicitly says heuristic/uncalibrated.

findings.title: Expected sales and revenue are derived from favorites without attributable sales
findings.explanation: _compute_roi converts expected favorites into expected sales using fixed ratios and then into expected revenue. commands_guide displays these as 'Expected Sales' and 'Expected Revenue'. There is no confirmed sales evidence for the candidate.
findings.reproduction: Static inspection of _compute_roi and the guide embed. The calculation is deterministic from favorite averages and price, not from my_sales or any attributable transaction.
findings.production_impact: Presents fabricated financial expectations as if they were measured, violating the evidence-integrity requirement.
findings.recommended_correction: Remove expected sales/revenue or explicitly label them as non-evidence speculative scenarios. Use confirmed attributable sales only when available.
findings.verification: Assert the guide never displays Expected Sales/Revenue without confirmed sales evidence; add regression tests for missing sales.

findings.title: Multiple direct Roblox API calls bypass the shared scheduler and circuit breaker
findings.file: commands_sales.py, commands_supercomputer.py, creative_pivot.py, desc_forge.py, recovery_brain.py, suggest.py, tag_generator.py
findings.explanation: These call sites use requests.get/post directly. They do not share execution_policy's rate bucket, in-flight dedupe, Retry-After handling, or circuit breaker. roblox_batch_client also has an independent token bucket and retry loop without the shared circuit.
findings.reproduction: Static search for requests.get/post outside execution_policy/live_market, plus inspection of roblox_batch_client.py:110-162. The production 429 history is consistent with multiple independent request sources.
findings.production_impact: Concurrent command and scheduler traffic can exceed intended API pacing and trigger account/IP rate limits. A circuit opened by one client does not protect the others.
findings.recommended_correction: Route all Roblox HTTP through one scheduler/client abstraction. Add a shared circuit breaker and Retry-After-aware pacing. Remove direct requests from commands and helper modules.
findings.verification: Fault-injection test that opens the circuit in one path and asserts every other path receives a deferred/no-request response. Count mocked HTTP calls across command suites.

findings.title: main is unprotected and every push auto-deploys without required CI
findings.explanation: GitHub reports main as protected=false. deploy.yml triggers on every push to main/master and runs git reset --hard, dependency installation, and service restart. Survival/PostgreSQL workflows only run on pull requests to main or selected feature branches; the frozen baseline main had only an auto-deploy run.
findings.reproduction: GET /repos/fiverrdev44-collab/robux-ugc-advanced/branches/main returns protected=false. GitHub Actions listing for branch main at 4399eae shows only Oracle Auto-Deploy; no survival or PostgreSQL run.
findings.production_impact: A direct push can deploy untested code to production. Local direct merges bypass mandatory PR checks.
findings.recommended_correction: Protect main, require pull requests and passing Survival/PostgreSQL checks, restrict who can push, and require manual environment approval for production deployment.
findings.verification: Attempt a direct push to main and confirm rejection; require the checks in branch protection settings.

findings.title: tracked_creators is keyed only by numeric creator_id, so User/Group collisions overwrite or merge
findings.explanation: tracked_creators has PRIMARY KEY (creator_id) with creator_type default 'User'. add_creator uses ON CONFLICT (creator_id) DO NOTHING, so a Group sharing a numeric ID with a User cannot be independently stored. ORACLE resolves creator types by numeric ID from this table.
findings.reproduction: Schema and SQL inspection. A disposable PostgreSQL insert of the same numeric ID with User and Group would collide because the primary key contains only creator_id.
findings.production_impact: Creator-type evidence can be misattributed; ORACLE cohort/type filters and creator analysis may use the wrong identity.
findings.recommended_correction: Migrate tracked_creators to a composite key (creator_type, creator_id) or add a separate typed identity table; update all reads/writes and preserve unknown type as unknown.
findings.verification: Disposable PostgreSQL test inserting the same numeric ID as User and Group; assert two independent rows and correct ORACLE type resolution.

findings.title: Creator Brain success cohorts and patterns group by display name, not stable identity
findings.explanation: Creator Brain groups by lower(creator_name). Display-name collisions merge unrelated creators, and creator renames split one creator. M2 introduced stable composite identities, but Creator Brain does not use them.
findings.reproduction: Static SQL inspection in creator_brain.py. This is the same class of identity risk M2 tests explicitly cover for creator_registry.
findings.production_impact: Success cohorts, verified/nonverified comparisons, and stored creator_patterns can be contaminated by name collisions or renames.
findings.recommended_correction: Use (creator_type, creator_id) from creator_registry/tracked creators for cohorts and patterns; use display names only as a fallback labeled approximation.
findings.verification: Disposable PostgreSQL fixture with same-name different-ID creators and one renamed creator; assert no merge/split contamination.

findings.title: A single discovery RateLimited aborts the entire ORACLE creator pass
findings.explanation: On RateLimited during discovery, the loop records discovery_rate_limited and breaks. If this happens on the first creator, creators_scanned and observations_inserted remain zero. Prior production audit evidence recorded this exact pattern for the first cohort creator.
findings.reproduction: Source inspection plus prior read-only production counters: creators_eligible=16, creators_scanned=0, observations_inserted=0, truncated_creators={'14349551':'discovery_rate_limited'}. No new production scan was run in M5.
findings.production_impact: Zero-observation scans; partial status; no creator learning progress while rate limits persist.
findings.recommended_correction: Isolate failures per creator, add a resumable discovery cursor or deterministic rotation, and keep the existing rate-limit budget. Do not blindly rescan all failed creators.
findings.verification: Unit test with a RateLimited first creator and subsequent success; assert later creators are scanned or a cursor resumes them without exceeding the budget.

findings.title: Mixed timestamp types create window and freshness ambiguity
findings.explanation: items.created_at and item_history.snapshot_at are TIMESTAMP without time zone, while queries compare them with NOW() (timestamptz) and use make_interval windows. Results depend on the session TimeZone.
findings.reproduction: Schema inspection in database.py. M4/M3 window queries use NOW() against these columns. get_db_connection sets TimeZone='UTC' for its own connections, but other callers may not.
findings.production_impact: A non-UTC session can shift 48h/180d window membership and freshness judgments.
findings.recommended_correction: Standardize on TIMESTAMPTZ/UTC or cast explicitly with documented semantics; add a session-timezone regression test.
findings.verification: Run window queries under UTC and a non-UTC TimeZone in disposable PostgreSQL; assert identical membership.

findings.title: Startup setup can destructively deduplicate sales without event-ID awareness
findings.explanation: When RUN_MIGRATIONS_ON_START=1, setup_database deletes my_sales rows sharing sale_time/item_name/buyer/amount, before the event-id indexes are ensured. The delete does not compare source_event_id, so distinct transactions with the same fingerprint can be removed.
findings.reproduction: Static SQL inspection. The M5 disposable probe could not execute setup_database because database.get_db_connection hardcodes sslmode=require; this remains a code-level risk rather than an observed production event.
findings.production_impact: Potential permanent loss of legitimate sales if the migrations-on-start flag is enabled.
findings.recommended_correction: Remove destructive startup dedupe. Perform dedupe only as an explicit, reviewed migration that considers source_event_id and is preceded by a backup.
findings.verification: Disposable PostgreSQL with SSL enabled: insert two distinct source_event_id rows with identical fingerprint, run setup twice, assert both rows remain.

findings.title: !concept cannot reach EXPERIMENT CANDIDATE because no M3 bundle is passed
findings.explanation: render_concept_request defaults m3_bundle=None, and commands_concept calls it without a bundle. _market_status returns EXPERIMENT CANDIDATE only when an M3 verdict is VALIDATE EXPERIMENTALLY. The command therefore cannot elevate a concept above INVESTIGATE from M3 evidence.
findings.reproduction: Static call-chain inspection. Unit tests pass only when an M3 bundle is injected directly; the command path has no injection.
findings.production_impact: M4 does not consume existing M3 opportunity evidence in normal Discord use; the strongest M4 status is unreachable.
findings.recommended_correction: Persist or pass the existing M3 evidence bundle into M4, or explicitly document that !concept is independent and remove the unreachable status claim. Do not add a live verification pass.
findings.verification: Command-level test with a stored M3 bundle and flag ON; assert the bundle reaches _market_status and the report reflects it.

findings.title: Command coverage matrix is stale and coverage is incomplete
findings.explanation: Runtime registration contains 90 commands; the matrix lists 84. Missing commands are concept, emote_title, help, link, outcome, and rename. The matrix marks 66 commands 'not exercised' and 5 'manual'; only 13 are marked automated.
findings.reproduction: Imported discord_ugc_bot with dummy TOKEN/DATABASE_URL and enumerated bot.commands; diff against the matrix. M5_COMMAND_MATRIX.csv records the full 90-command runtime registry.
findings.production_impact: Release confidence is overstated; command failures or authorization gaps can ship without coverage.
findings.recommended_correction: Regenerate the matrix from runtime registration in CI, add command-metadata tests, and classify each command as read-only/mutating/owner-only.
findings.verification: CI job compares runtime registry to the committed matrix and fails on drift.

findings.title: M4 has no M3 integration and AI debug performs unbudgeted provider calls
findings.explanation: !ai_debug performs live Gemini/OpenRouter calls outside the AI-reasoning budget. !concept performs one AI call per invocation without rate limiting. These are additional cost/abuse surfaces.
findings.reproduction: Source inspection. ai_debug calls client.models.generate_content and chat.completions.create directly; concept calls the AI generator without a per-user quota.
findings.production_impact: Quota exhaustion and unexpected provider spend from repeated Discord invocations.
findings.recommended_correction: Owner-gate diagnostics, use a bounded budget, and rate-limit per-user AI generation.
findings.verification: Unit test with a fake provider; assert denied users/over-limit requests make zero provider calls.

findings.title: Dependencies and deployment actions are unpinned
findings.explanation: requirements.txt has no version constraints; deploy.yml uses appleboy/ssh-action@master and ignores dependency-install failures with '|| true'. Other workflows install unpinned packages.
findings.production_impact: Non-reproducible builds and supply-chain risk; a failed dependency install can leave production on stale packages.
findings.recommended_correction: Pin Python packages and actions to reviewed versions/digests; fail the deploy on dependency errors.
findings.verification: CI dependency check with a lockfile/hash; deploy dry run fails on install error.

findings.title: Importing the bot module starts the background scheduler
findings.explanation: start_scheduler() runs at module import, not under an application factory or __main__ guard. Importing the module for diagnostics/tests starts scheduler threads; a double import/duplicate process can start duplicate jobs.
findings.reproduction: M5 runtime command enumeration imported discord_ugc_bot and observed APScheduler jobs being scheduled and a snapshot catch-up DB attempt.
findings.production_impact: Duplicate or unintended scheduled work in tooling/testing; harder isolation of command registration.
findings.recommended_correction: Move scheduler startup behind __main__ or an explicit application factory; make registration import side-effect free.
findings.verification: Import test asserts no scheduler jobs are created; application startup test asserts exactly one scheduler.

findings.title: DB Check workflow prints database host/name/user to CI logs
findings.explanation: The manual workflow prints DB host, database name, and username. It is read-only but exposes environment metadata to anyone who can read workflow logs.
findings.recommended_correction: Redact host/user/database or print only connectivity/status.
findings.verification: Workflow log contains no host/user/database strings.
